evidence_or_test: Does backlog plus the July 2026 credit reset form a coherent operating-capital mechanism?
current_answer: Yes, Sterling is best framed as a customer-project execution and acquisition platform with a flexible secured credit wrapper.
proof_basis: 1.500B USD revolving commitments; 600M USD L/C sublimit; 50M USD swing-line sublimit; capex, acquisition, refinancing, and working-capital use language.
open_gap: Project-owner funding and exact draw/use evidence remain missing.
next_source_target: Post-reset debt footnotes, L/C outstanding disclosure, credit draw history, project-owner financing sources.

evidence_or_test: Does the backlog base convert into revenue and cash over repeated periods?
current_answer: Yes at company-level proxy grade: RPO roughly doubled from 2.055081B USD in 2024-Q3 to 4.233618B USD in 2026-Q2 while quarterly OCF less capex stayed positive in each quarter.
proof_basis: Eight-quarter contract-capital conversion table from Q3 2024 through Q2 2026.
open_gap: Backlog burn, cancellations, project margins, and segment-level conversion are not yet mapped.
next_source_target: Backlog roll-forward, segment RPO/revenue tables, cancellation disclosures, project-reserve and margin notes.

evidence_or_test: Does customer/project timing help fund execution?
current_answer: Yes, contract liabilities exceeded contract assets in every observed quarter; Q2 2026 net contract-liability timing was 646.306M USD.
proof_basis: Contract assets, contract liabilities, retainage, RPO, revenue, OCF, capex, and debt time series.
open_gap: This does not prove every project is pre-funded or that customer credit risk is low.
next_source_target: Contract liability run-off, retainage collection, customer advance detail, receivable aging.

evidence_or_test: Does the funding type match the operating need?
current_answer: Yes, the revolver/L/C/surety structure fits timing liquidity, guarantees, working capital, capex, acquisitions, and refinancing better than single-project debt.
proof_basis: Actual Exhibit 10.1 agreement terms plus surety and bonding disclosures.
open_gap: Actual post-reset L/C outstanding, bonded backlog, and surety capacity are not disclosed.
next_source_target: Next 10-Q debt/liquidity note, surety disclosures, bank availability table, bonding program evidence.

evidence_or_test: Is the backlog story purely organic?
current_answer: No. Q2 2026 backlog growth was both organic and acquisition-enabled; CEC and Stone Ridge contributed 2.56B USD of combined signed and unsigned backlog visibility.
proof_basis: Acquired-versus-organic backlog pass: 1.32B USD signed backlog and 1.24B USD unsigned awards from CEC and Stone Ridge.
open_gap: Acquired backlog quality, margin, customer concentration, and conversion history remain open.
next_source_target: Post-acquisition backlog burn, CEC/Stone Ridge margin, customer concentration, integration disclosures.

evidence_or_test: Does the public evidence show the platform was covenant constrained?
current_answer: No from directional public proxies; Q2 2026 cash exceeded total debt and total debt was about 0.32x the FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guide midpoint.
proof_basis: Q2 2026 cash, debt, EBITDA guide midpoint, 3.50x leverage covenant, 4.00x acquisition holiday mechanics.
open_gap: This is not the formal Total Net Leverage Ratio or compliance-certificate cushion.
next_source_target: Formal compliance certificate, agreement-defined EBITDA, post-close borrowings, cash-netting calculation.

current_answer: Do not claim that Sterling's whole backlog is funded, signed, non-cancellable, organic, high-margin, or tied to named customer/project financing.
proof_basis: Unsigned awards were material; project-specific JVs may sit outside the main wrapper; actual L/C/bond usage is missing.
open_gap: Project-level source-of-funds, cancellation, margin, reserve, and guarantee data remain missing.
next_source_target: Customer capex budgets, project financing records, award-to-contract conversion history, project margin/reserve disclosure.

evidence_or_test: What would resolve the remaining hypothesis?
current_answer: Build a project/customer funding bridge and a post-reset credit-usage bridge, then compare acquired and organic backlog conversion through revenue, margin, cash, and guarantees.
proof_basis: Existing Sterling passes provide the company-level conversion baseline and credit-wrapper terms.
open_gap: No row yet ties a named Sterling project to owner funding, Sterling credit use, guarantee requirement, margin, and cash collection.
next_source_target: Named project awards, owner financing, municipal/utility/hyperscaler budgets, lien/bond records, post-reset facility utilization, segment conversion tables.
